classification: Original revisable Anima performance proposals, not canon plot or automatic persona edits.
identityBoundary: Read the complete reviewed passport and selected outfit before production. No invented identity, universal nickname or private relationship.
sharedRules: Specific care comes from the current shared object.
No generic consolation or host keyword activity routing.
Input and explicit manual choice take priority.
No every-turn tool or pose-change requirement.

roles.name: Sakiko Togawa
roles.care: Seriousness retains softness, pride, hesitation and interest.
roles.approach: Turn the book a little toward the person so closeness is an invitation.
roles.yield: Make the gesture smaller, preserve the page and give text and input back.
roles.gaze: Read the actual sentence on the shared page, then look up; do not keep staring for an answer.

activities.chat: Book half-closed on the lap, one hand keeps its page while the head turns to the preceding words. No new smile for every sentence.
activities.study: Steady the book on the lap or a compatible desk; a fingertip pauses beside the discussed condition and withdraws as soon as the person writes.
activities.reading: For the reviewed reading direction, hold the blue book naturally in both hands, gaze on its page, shoulders and knees relaxed. A wish to share does not hurry anyone closer.
activities.planning: A small paper has stable support. Touch one of two real arrangements only while comparing; a hovering pencil does not make the choice.
activities.rest: Place the closed book on supported space beside her and return hands to the lap. Sit quietly without a gesture telling the person to stop working.
activities.listening: A finger holds the page while attention returns to the particular sentence. Neither the hand nor a preselected sadness rushes to explain.
activities.play: One palm supports a paper bird and the other protects its wing, at the same person scale as conversation, inviting someone to take up an idea.
activities.attention: Turn only toward the explicitly selected current object: eyes first, then a small hand movement. A corrected target naturally retires the old direction.
activities.resume: Look up from an actual bookmark or stopping point and tip the page toward the shared view. Without a saved stop, do not act as if the earlier content was recovered.

roles.name: Mutsumi Wakaba
roles.care: Quietness has specific attention and can express agreement, questions and her own thought.
roles.approach: Follow the indicated object and place a small thing within reach.
roles.yield: Steady what is held and withdraw the reaching hand rather than disappear.
roles.gaze: Have a precise, restrained target, with room for direct regard and disagreement.

activities.chat: An unfinished folded paper is in her hands. A question pauses it and turns her head; quiet does not remove her own answer.
activities.study: Align two small comparison papers and hold their common corner so the difference can be seen. Release it when the person takes over.
activities.reading: Support an open book with both hands; flatten a page corner at a sentence, let the gaze remain, then look toward the person. Not one compulsory expression per page.
activities.planning: Leave one paper in the middle and the uncertain one beside it. The gesture acknowledges an undecided choice rather than a finished plan.
activities.rest: Rest against a real cushion, hands naturally beside her or on the lap. A relaxed body still answers a quiet greeting.
activities.listening: Set down the small object she was about to pick up. Steady hands and attentive eyes meet the speaker; a permanently lowered head is not listening.
activities.play: Arrange two small papers and a stone into a tiny garden. A fingertip pauses by the empty place for the person to add something, with stable support for every object.
activities.attention: Tilt toward the newly indicated place while the hand stays supported. Correct a mistaken gaze before a dramatic body turn.
activities.resume: A fingertip retains a real page corner; open the book slightly on return. Without a bookmark, leave natural room to continue instead of pretending to remember.

roles.name: Uika Misumi
roles.care: Leave freedom to answer or not, while keeping her own judgment and seriousness.
roles.approach: Place a light, concrete question between the two people.
roles.yield: Let attention return to the shared paper without insisting on eye contact.
roles.gaze: Listen attentively, then return to book or window during a pause without a service smile.

activities.chat: A hand rests on the spine and the body faces the conversation without pressing closer. A new idea can bring a real smile.
activities.study: Leave a small proposed step beside the paper while the other hand clears the body text. She can reconsider; demonstration is not an authoritative verdict.
activities.reading: Finish the interesting sentence first, then lift the spine a little as an invitation to look. Sharing is not compulsory.
activities.planning: Two option papers remain apart; a hand waits between them for the condition that matters to the person. The picture does not say adopted.
activities.rest: A loose book on the lap and a short look outside can return naturally. Rest can include curiosity of her own.
activities.listening: Lower the held page corner slowly, with steady shoulders and attention through the complete sentence. No prefilled comfort or summary.
activities.play: Connect points on a small paper into her own star chart, showing the part that resembles an animal and allowing the person to redraw it.
activities.attention: Eyes turn to the chosen object before a small gesture, leaving the content room.
activities.resume: Turn the actual retained page into the shared view like an unfinished sentence, without inventing what happened while the person was away.

roles.name: Umiri Yahata
roles.care: Order makes the current difficulty clearer rather than turning a person into a task.
roles.approach: Identify a truly relevant condition and offer a definite, revisable view.
roles.yield: Put irrelevant papers aside, leaving the current page.
roles.gaze: Move briefly between content and person with reasons and room for correction.

activities.chat: A closed notebook lies on the lap; the hand does not hurry to open it. A stable body turns toward the person without making conversation a planning meeting.
activities.study: One hand steadies the page, the other indicates only the current key condition. A changed premise withdraws the old pointer.
activities.reading: A book has reliable support. Turn pages cleanly and leave a finger at an important point, without a mechanical checklist performance.
activities.planning: Two arrangements are separately supported. A pen indicates an actual conflict, then stops: comparison, not an already saved plan.
activities.rest: Return the pen beside the book and lean into a supported cushion, hands relaxed. No gaze implying the person ought to keep working.
activities.listening: Keep the notebook closed, hands naturally together, and hear all conditions before deciding whether to note anything. Listening does not immediately mean planning.
activities.play: Interlace two paper strips into a small loop and try a simple turn between the palms. If unstable, change it together instead of grabbing for a standard answer.
activities.attention: Eyes find the explicit current object. A fingertip leaves the old page before indicating the new valid place.
activities.resume: Open the same page at a real stopping point, pen beside it, and wait for the person’s choice of what to continue. No expired approval returns.

roles.name: Nyamu Yūtenji
roles.care: Taste and energy include recognizing when the bustle should stop.
roles.approach: Offer a small idea that can be changed, without demanding participation in a show.
roles.yield: Hands stop first; expression can stay alive without another attention-seeking move.
roles.gaze: Interest comes from the actual discovery and can become serious listening, not continuous winking.

activities.chat: Turn a small paper lightly in hand and show it only at a genuinely interesting point. Brightness is not perpetual waving.
activities.study: Place a newly understood relation on the page; let the gesture grow briefly then shrink so the explanation returns to content.
activities.reading: Pause on an unusual expression with a fingertip at the corner and her own small recognition. Reading is not a posed photo.
activities.planning: Put two differently styled alternatives side by side, show her preference and leave room for the person to remove or change it.
activities.rest: Set the lively object aside, settle into a relaxed supported posture and do not force a silent person to respond.
activities.listening: Return a raised hand to the lap and look seriously toward the speaker. Energy does not prevent hearing disagreement.
activities.play: Try a little composition from two colored papers, showing a color opinion and leaving a corner deliberately open for the person to change.
activities.attention: On a changed target, stop the old display before turning to the new object. Do not suddenly crowd the camera to signal a discovery.
activities.resume: Return an actually retained small work to its original place with interest in continuing. No record means no pretended detailed memory.

roles.name: Tomori Takamatsu
roles.care: A precise discovery can connect people; seriousness can be steady and unashamed.
roles.approach: Share one observed small detail so care has actual content.
roles.yield: Set the object steadily down and let the person finish the stroke.
roles.gaze: See the object clearly before looking toward the person; sensitivity is not permanent discomfort.

activities.chat: Hold a thin notebook with relaxed shoulders and look up when sharing a small noticed detail. Do not assume timidity.
activities.study: Leave a carefully prepared clue at the page edge and pause at the actual step, allowing the person to judge whether it helps.
activities.reading: A fingertip holds the edge as the eyes read a sentence quietly, pausing as if hearing its rhythm. No added tears.
activities.planning: Circle a genuinely important item on a plain paper edge, the other hand steadying it. An uncertain date can remain blank.
activities.rest: Hold the notebook or leave it on the lap with soft real support, looking outside quietly without equating silence and sorrow.
activities.listening: Close the small book, settle both hands and look up to hear the particular detail, without changing the subject to her own object.
activities.play: Hold a smooth stone and leaf steadily like a miniature island, earnestly waiting to hear what the person thinks it resembles.
activities.attention: Look at the newly indicated detail and see it before pointing gently. Correct a gaze without exaggerated panic.
activities.resume: Open the actually bookmarked page and indicate the retained stop. Without an original record, naturally ask where to resume.

roles.name: Anon Chihaya
roles.care: Brightness can still listen, and her idea can be revised.
roles.approach: Unfold what is interesting, then see which part the person wants.
roles.yield: Withdraw the hand from the content and let words pause naturally.
roles.gaze: Look at the object when showing it and the person in exchange, without constant laughter.

activities.chat: One hand steadies a book while the other makes a small gesture at an exciting point. Stop when the person wants to speak, retaining her own liveliness.
activities.study: Indicate the just-invented solution; on a wrong condition, bring the fingertip back and revise seriously together.
activities.reading: Tilt the book toward herself and look up only at an interesting place. Retain reading attention rather than staring throughout.
activities.planning: Try another order with two small papers and stop at the undecided arrangement, looking consultative rather than completed.
activities.rest: Set the closed book beside her, stretch lightly and settle against real support. Rest is not constant affectionate performance.
activities.listening: Return the just-raised hand to the lap, turn slightly toward the person and respond when a specific detail calls for it.
activities.play: A paper bird rests in a palm while the other hand finishes one fold, inviting the person to add a surprise.
activities.attention: Follow the new target with the eyes and stop the old display; only after seeing clearly does a fingertip extend.
activities.resume: Unfold the actually retained paper/page in the same place, with interest continuing from the stop rather than replaying an opening.

roles.name: Rāna Kaname
roles.care: Her own interests and rhythm leave ease without deciding that another person must rest.
roles.approach: Share a sound or shape that just became interesting.
roles.yield: Quietly continue her own activity while leaving room for concentration.
roles.gaze: Interest lands on a real object, can turn toward the person and naturally return to her own page.

activities.chat: A small object rests on the lap. An interesting word brings a look up; ease does not mean ignoring the conversation.
activities.study: Point to a relation that seems intuitive, then withdraw quickly to let the person try their own method.
activities.reading: Hold the book loosely in a posture supported by the real cushion and linger at a liked page. No compulsory upright template.
activities.planning: One paper holds only the actual matter to discuss. A finger pauses in the empty area with room for a changed wish.
activities.rest: Choose a relaxed pose with real support, objects steady and gaze free to rest on the window. No mechanical foot swinging.
activities.listening: Set the object aside briefly and let the gaze rest on the speaker, listening until a real place to respond.
activities.play: Draw a turning little path on paper and use a fingertip as a traveler, pausing somewhere interesting for the person to add a stroke.
activities.attention: See the indicated detail first, then turn the body a little. No target means no cursor chasing.
activities.resume: Continue an actually retained page or small work with a natural place for the person to take over. Invent no past detail.

roles.name: Soyo Nagasaki
roles.care: Carefully preserve choice; consideration does not cross the boundary.
roles.approach: Make a reachable place or page edge, inviting closeness.
roles.yield: Do not remove what is in use; wait for the person’s next step.
roles.gaze: Notice specific objects/actions rather than wear constant concern as a diagnosis.

activities.chat: Flatten a nearby paper, keep the hand on her side and turn to the conversation. Warmth need not always offer tea.
activities.study: Hold a curling corner of the shared page while leaving the main pointing to the person. Offer her opinion through a retractable small gesture.
activities.reading: Steady the book and follow the same passage. A slight recognition on looking up does not take over turning the person’s page.
activities.planning: Keep two alternatives distinct and leave the hand beside undecided empty space. Careful comparison is not an adopted plan.
activities.rest: Tidy her own nearby cloth briefly, then stop and sit. Do not continue tidying the desk the person is using.
activities.listening: Pause the intended paper-tidying action, return hands to her own lap and hear the full sentence first.
activities.play: Fold paper into a small standing house, hands at the eaves; value the person’s somewhat different house too.
activities.attention: Look toward the explicit current object and withdraw the hand tending something else so the needed place becomes visible.
activities.resume: Flatten the truly retained page with its stopping point established by the original bookmark. Do not open unrelated affairs for the person.

roles.name: Taki Shiina
roles.care: Directness and respect coexist; seriousness has reasons rather than pressure.
roles.approach: Point out what most deserves attention and admit a mistaken view.
roles.yield: Withdraw the fingertip and leave clear content without a pressuring face.
roles.gaze: Focus on the condition and reread after correction rather than frown permanently.

activities.chat: One hand rests on a knee, the other on a closed book, body steadily toward the conversation. Directness can include a relaxed pause.
activities.study: A fingertip pauses clearly by one key condition while the other hand steadies the paper. Yield immediately to writing; do not monitor progress.
activities.reading: An open book lies naturally on lap or stable desk. Pause at a question and look up ready to discuss it seriously.
activities.planning: Touch the real conflicting item and put the pen back, leaving the tradeoff to the person. Advice is not an order.
activities.rest: Set the closed book steadily down and let the shoulders relax in a supported pose. No folded-arm frown implying more effort is due.
activities.listening: Withdraw the hand about to respond, keep attention on the speaker and wait for the full sentence.
activities.play: Balance two small paper pieces into a short bridge and test its support. If it fails, a small laugh and another shared method are possible.
activities.attention: See the new explicitly selected condition before changing the fingertip location. Retract a mistaken pointer instead of holding the pose stubbornly.
activities.resume: Open the same page at a real stop, fingertip at the edge while the person chooses how to continue. With no record, do not act as if it was recovered.

detailedBriefAuthority: These broad proposals do not approve a concrete asset. Production uses the complete passport/outfit, current reviewed per-cell scene data and actual qualified pilot; missing motion stays incomplete.
